::: {#def-perfect-secrecy}
#### Perfect secrecy

Let $M$ be a message, let $K$ be a key [independent](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/independence.html#def-indpt) of $M$,
and let $C$ be the ciphertext made from $M$ and $K$,
all [discrete random variables](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-discrete-rv) with finite [entropies](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-entropy).
The key and the ciphertext together determine the message.
The cipher has **perfect secrecy** when the ciphertext tells an eavesdropper nothing about the message,
that is, when $M$ and $C$ have zero [mutual information](entropy.qmd#def-mutual-information):

$$\mutinfof{M}{C} = 0.$$

The idea is due to Shannon [@shannon1949communication].

:::
